# Proof of possession (DPoP)

<!-- Generated by internal/apidoc from the packages' doc comments: edit those, then run `task docs:api`. -->

Binding a capability to a key (RFC 9449): proofs, nonces and the replay caches. Part of the [API reference](README.md).

<a id="dpop"></a><a id="package-dpop"></a>

## Package dpop

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/dpop"`

Package dpop implements proof of possession after RFC 9449 (DPoP): a client signs a short JWT over each request with a key it holds, and a server checks the proof against the key a token is bound to. It depends on no token format: the server says which thumbprint the key must have and which access token the proof must name.

An authorization server's token endpoint checks the proof a token request carries with CheckTokenRequest, and binds what it issues to the key that signed it (RFC 9449 §5).

<a id="dpop.ErrorCodeInvalidProof"></a><a id="dpop.ErrorCodeUseNonce"></a>

### dpop.ErrorCodeInvalidProof, dpop.ErrorCodeUseNonce

```go
const (
	// ErrorCodeInvalidProof answers ErrRequired, ErrInvalid and ErrReplayed.
	ErrorCodeInvalidProof = "invalid_dpop_proof"
	// ErrorCodeUseNonce answers ErrNonceRequired.
	ErrorCodeUseNonce = "use_dpop_nonce"
)
```

The error codes RFC 9449 gives a refused proof, on the wire of a resource server's challenge (§7.1) and of a token endpoint's response (§5, §8).

<a id="dpop.HMACNonceKeyBytes"></a><a id="dpop.DefaultNonceLifetime"></a><a id="dpop.HMACNonceClockSkew"></a>

### dpop.HMACNonceKeyBytes, dpop.DefaultNonceLifetime, dpop.HMACNonceClockSkew

```go
const (
	// HMACNonceKeyBytes is the least key length NewHMACNonces accepts: the
	// output size of the HMAC's hash.
	HMACNonceKeyBytes = sha256.Size
	// DefaultNonceLifetime is how long a nonce is accepted when the
	// configuration names no lifetime.
	DefaultNonceLifetime = 5 * time.Minute
	// HMACNonceClockSkew is how far ahead of a replica's clock a nonce's
	// issuance may lie: another replica's clock may run ahead, and the
	// issuance is kept to the second.
	HMACNonceClockSkew = 5 * time.Second
)
```

HMACNonce sizes and defaults.

<a id="dpop.ReplayClockSkew"></a>

### dpop.ReplayClockSkew

```go
const ReplayClockSkew = 5 * time.Second
```

ReplayClockSkew is how much longer than its acceptance window a proof's id is remembered (ReplayEntry.ExpiresAt): a replay cache reads its own clock, a moment after the verifier — or, shared, a different machine's — and must still hold the id of every proof the verifier could accept.

<sub>[dpop/dpop.go](../../dpop/dpop.go)</sub>
<a id="dpop.ErrRequired"></a><a id="dpop.ErrInvalid"></a><a id="dpop.ErrReplayed"></a><a id="dpop.ErrReplayQuota"></a>

### dpop.ErrRequired, dpop.ErrInvalid, dpop.ErrReplayed, dpop.ErrReplayQuota

```go
var (
	// ErrRequired — the token is key-bound and no proof came with it.
	ErrRequired = errors.New("dpop: proof required")
	// ErrInvalid — a proof came, and it does not prove possession for this
	// token, method, URL and moment.
	ErrInvalid = errors.New("dpop: invalid proof")
	// ErrReplayed — a proof's jti was already used inside the window.
	ErrReplayed = errors.New("dpop: proof replayed")
	// ErrReplayQuota — the proof may be good, and its holder already has as
	// many live proof ids as the replay cache keeps for one holder, or the
	// cache is full: it is refused unrecorded, since an id not recorded could
	// be replayed. Not a replay and not the proof's fault: the same request,
	// signed afresh, passes once older ids lapse. RFC 9449 names no code for
	// it, so ErrorCodeInvalidProof does not answer it.
	ErrReplayQuota = errors.New("dpop: replay cache quota exhausted")
)
```

The refusals of a proof. A caller that judges what they mean for the request — limes reads each as a refusal of the credentials — wraps them. Verify returns one of them, ErrNonceRequired, ErrReplayQuota, an error naming a Request it cannot check (no Token or no Holder), or a failure of the replay cache or the nonces, which is not a refusal of the proof.

### dpop.Sign

```go
func Sign(ctx context.Context, key crypto.Signer, req SignRequest) (string, error)
```

Sign signs a proof for one request. key is any crypto.Signer whose public key is Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256; one that also has SignContext is given ctx, so a slow or cancelled remote signature is bounded by it. A request without IssuedAt, a URL that is no absolute URI with a host or that carries userinfo, or a key of another type is limes.ErrInvalidRequest.

<a id="dpop.HMACNonces"></a>

### dpop.HMACNonces

```go
type HMACNonces struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

HMACNonces is a Nonces that keeps no state: a nonce is its issuance time and an HMAC of it, so every replica holding the same keys issues and accepts the same nonces. A nonce is not bound to the client it was sent to, nor used up by a proof: it limits how long before use a proof can be signed to its lifetime, so keep Lifetime as short as the clients' round trip allows. Rotate by putting the new key first: it issues, and the old ones, kept in Keys until their nonces expire, still accept them.

<a id="dpop.MemoryReplayCache"></a>

### dpop.MemoryReplayCache

```go
type MemoryReplayCache struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

MemoryReplayCache is a bounded in-process ReplayCache. A deployment with several replicas behind a balancer that does not pin a client to one replica can see a proof replayed on another replica within the window; keep the window short, use server nonces (VerifierConfig.Nonces), or back ReplayCache with a shared store — the redisreplay module ships one over Redis.

Every holder gets a share of the cache of its own (EntriesPerHolder), so one capability cannot fill it with proofs and lock every other one out — not even a Biscuit whose copies are bound to as many keys as their holder likes, since they are one capability: past its share, only its proofs are refused. It does not stop one tenant holding many capabilities — Delegate mints them freely — from filling the cache with its proofs; past MaxEntries the cache refuses every new id rather than forget one, since a forgotten id could be replayed. Size MaxEntries for the busiest window. Server nonces (VerifierConfig.Nonces) do not bound it: an HMACNonces nonce may back any number of proofs until it expires, so they bound how early a proof is signed, not how many are.

A holder's share caps its rate: an id is kept until ReplayClockSkew past the end of its proof's window, which starts at the proof's iat, so one holder sending fresh proofs passes at most EntriesPerHolder of them over the window plus ReplayClockSkew — with the defaults 1,000 per 65 s, about 15 a second. A proof dated earlier within the window is kept for less, down to ReplayClockSkew. Past the share Seen returns ErrReplayQuota and logs the holder at WARN.

It keys a proof id by the key that signed it (jkt, jti) across holders, where redisreplay keys it within its holder: the same id under one key for two capabilities is refused here and accepted there. Neither is a replay — ath binds a proof to one token, and so to one holder.

<a id="dpop.MemoryReplayCache.Seen"></a>

#### dpop.MemoryReplayCache.Seen

```go
func (c *MemoryReplayCache) Seen(ctx context.Context, e ReplayEntry) (bool, error)
```

Seen implements ReplayCache. Expired ids are dropped as they lapse, soonest first, so a full cache costs a lookup rather than a scan. A holder past its share, or a cache full of live ids, refuses the new id with ErrReplayQuota rather than accept it unrecorded — a full cache errs towards refusing.

<a id="dpop.ReplayCache"></a>

### dpop.ReplayCache

```go
type ReplayCache interface {
	// Seen records e and reports whether its id was already recorded. A
	// holder that has used its share of the cache, or a cache with no room
	// left, returns an error wrapping ErrReplayQuota, and logs it: the proof
	// is refused rather than accepted unrecorded, and not as a replay. A
	// cache that cannot answer — its store unreachable — returns another
	// error, and Verify refuses the proof with it.
	Seen(ctx context.Context, e ReplayEntry) (bool, error)
}
```

ReplayCache remembers proof ids for as long as a proof could be accepted.

<sub>[dpop/dpop.go](../../dpop/dpop.go)</sub>
<a id="dpop.Verifier.Check"></a>

#### dpop.Verifier.Check

```go
func (v *Verifier) Check(ctx context.Context, req Request) (CheckedProof, error)
```

Check is everything Verify checks but whether the proof's jti is new: it records nothing in the replay cache. A caller with checks of its own to make between the two — a revocation lookup — runs them after Check and calls Record only once they pass, so a proof is recorded only for a request that is otherwise accepted, and the cheap refusals come first.

<sub>[dpop/dpop.go](../../dpop/dpop.go)</sub>
<a id="dpop.Verifier.CheckTokenRequest"></a>

#### dpop.Verifier.CheckTokenRequest

```go
func (v *Verifier) CheckTokenRequest(ctx context.Context, req TokenRequest) (CheckedProof, error)
```

CheckTokenRequest is Check for a proof sent to a token endpoint: every check Check makes, except that the proof must name no access token (no ath) and may be by any key. The CheckedProof's JKT is that key's thumbprint, to bind the issued token to; Record records the proof once the endpoint's own checks pass.

```go
func (v *Verifier) Record(ctx context.Context, p CheckedProof) error
```

Record records a proof Check accepted in the replay cache, refusing it with ErrReplayed when its jti was seen before, and with the cache's error wrapping ErrReplayQuota when its holder has no room left in it. A CheckedProof Check did not make is limes.ErrInvalidRequest.

<sub>[dpop/dpop.go](../../dpop/dpop.go)</sub>
<a id="dpop.Verifier.Verify"></a>

#### dpop.Verifier.Verify

```go
func (v *Verifier) Verify(ctx context.Context, req Request) error
```

Verify checks req.Proof against the key req.Token is bound to. It passes only with a proof that: is no longer than MaxProofBytes; is a dpop+jwt with no crit header, signed by the public key its header carries; whose key's thumbprint is req.JKT; that names this method and URL and this token's hash; that was issued within the window; that carries a nonce Nonces accepts, when configured; and whose jti, no longer than MaxJTIBytes, is new. It is Check followed by Record.

<sub>[dpop/dpop.go](../../dpop/dpop.go)</sub>
<a id="dpop.VerifierConfig"></a>

### dpop.VerifierConfig

```go
type VerifierConfig struct {
	// Window bounds |now − iat|. Zero: DefaultWindow; negative is refused.
	Window time.Duration
	// Replay refuses a jti seen before. Required: without it a captured
	// proof is good for the whole window.
	Replay ReplayCache
	// Now is the clock. Nil: time.Now.
	Now func() time.Time
	// Nonces, when set, requires every proof to carry a nonce it issued
	// (RFC 9449 §8); a proof without a valid one is refused with
	// ErrNonceRequired, and Nonce gives the nonce to send back.
	Nonces Nonces
	// MaxProofBytes bounds the proof, refused unread past it. Zero:
	// DefaultMaxProofBytes; negative is refused.
	MaxProofBytes int
	// MatchPathOnly compares only the path of Proof.URL, and lets the
	// proof's path carry extra leading segments — for a server behind a
	// proxy, which cannot know the scheme, host or mount prefix its clients
	// address it by. The root path "/" is the exception: it must match
	// exactly, since as a tail it would match every path that ends in a
	// slash, so a server mounted under a prefix cannot take proofs at its
	// root.
	MatchPathOnly bool
}
```

VerifierConfig configures a Verifier. Zero fields take the defaults named on them; Replay is required.

<sub>[dpop/dpop.go](../../dpop/dpop.go)</sub>

<a id="redisreplay"></a><a id="package-redisreplay"></a>

## Package redisreplay

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/redisreplay"`

Package redisreplay is a dpop.ReplayCache over Redis, for a verifier that runs as several replicas: a proof replayed against any of them is refused, which an in-process dpop.MemoryReplayCache cannot promise.

It is a module of its own so that limes itself never depends on a Redis client.

#### Layout

Each holder has one sorted set, KeyPrefix followed by the holder, whose members are the proof ids recorded against it and whose scores are when they lapse. One call touches that one key, in one script, so a call is atomic and the cache works unchanged on Redis Cluster.

Ids are remembered per holder, not across holders. That loses nothing: a proof names the access token it was made for (its \`ath\`), and dpop.Verifier.Verify refuses it with any other token before the cache is asked, so a captured proof cannot reach the cache under another holder.

#### Clocks

What is live is decided by Config.Now, the verifier's clock, which every call sends to the script. Redis's own clock only runs the key's TTL, a duration that collects a holder gone quiet; a server clock running ahead cannot drop a live id.

The verifiers' clocks must agree to within dpop.ReplayClockSkew. An id is kept until ReplayClockSkew past the last instant a verifier accepts its proof, and each call drops the ids that have lapsed by its own clock: a replica running further ahead than that drops an id while a replica behind it still accepts the proof, which can then be replayed there. Keep the replicas on NTP.

#### Memory

EntriesPerHolder bounds each holder, and so its rate: an id is kept until dpop.ReplayClockSkew past the end of its proof's window, which starts at the proof's iat, so one holder sending fresh proofs passes at most EntriesPerHolder of them over the window plus dpop.ReplayClockSkew — with the defaults 1,000 per 65 s, about 15 a second. A proof dated earlier within the window is kept for less, down to dpop.ReplayClockSkew. Past the bound Seen returns dpop.ErrReplayQuota and logs the holder at WARN. Nothing bounds the holders. Bound the whole cache with Redis's maxmemory and the noeviction policy: past it a write fails, Seen returns the error and the proof is refused. An eviction policy would forget live ids, and a forgotten id can be replayed.

#### Failover

Redis replicates asynchronously, so ids a primary acknowledged and lost before a replica had them are forgotten when the replica takes over: a proof recorded there can be replayed once, inside its window. Keep dpop.VerifierConfig.Window short, or require server nonces (dpop.VerifierConfig.Nonces), where that matters.

<sub>[redisreplay/redisreplay.go](../../redisreplay/redisreplay.go)</sub>
<a id="redisreplay.Cache.Seen"></a>

#### redisreplay.Cache.Seen

```go
func (c *Cache) Seen(ctx context.Context, e dpop.ReplayEntry) (bool, error)
```

Seen implements dpop.ReplayCache. A holder past its share is refused with dpop.ErrReplayQuota, and logged at WARN, rather than accepted unrecorded; a Redis that cannot answer returns the error, and dpop.Verifier.Verify fails with it: an outage, not a refused proof.

<sub>[redisreplay/redisreplay.go](../../redisreplay/redisreplay.go)</sub>
<a id="redisreplay.Config"></a>

### redisreplay.Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Client runs the cache's script: a *redis.Client, *redis.ClusterClient,
	// *redis.Ring or any redis.UniversalClient. Required.
	Client redis.Scripter
	// KeyPrefix starts every key the cache writes. Zero: DefaultKeyPrefix.
	KeyPrefix string
	// EntriesPerHolder bounds the live proof ids of one holder. Zero:
	// dpop.DefaultReplayEntriesPerHolder.
	EntriesPerHolder int
	// Now is the clock. Nil: time.Now.
	Now func() time.Time
	// Logger logs each id refused because its holder's share is full, at
	// WARN, and a script answer the cache does not know, at ERROR. Nil:
	// slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger
}
```

Config configures a Cache.
